chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say:

Regarding a man who sought from a woman, unlawfully, access to her person, and she struck him with a stone and hit a fatal spot on him, he said: “There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if she were brought before a just Imam, he would deem his blood without liability.”

key_terms.أَهْدَرَ دَمَهُ: he would rule his blood uncompensated, with no liability for it
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ: a just Imam exercising legitimate judicial authority
key_terms.رَاوَدَ: he sought to seduce or compel unlawfully
key_terms.عَلَى نَفْسِهَا: against her person, meaning her bodily/sexual inviolability
key_terms.مَقْتَلًا: a fatal spot or lethal blow

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman kills a man while defending herself from unlawful assault?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who kills a man while defending herself from unlawful sexual aggression. It states that she bears no blame before Allah, and that a just Imam would not impose blood-liability for the aggressor’s death.
